thread.title_full: Transitions Healthcare Gettysburg receives 3-star CMS rating in 2026's first quarter

author: d. a. neumann
title: Transitions Healthcare Gettysburg receives 3-star CMS rating in 2026's first quarter
text:
Transitions Healthcare Gettysburg, as of the first quarter of 2026, was owned by Marc Feldman, Matthew Maurano, and Kevin Williams, according to Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS). Located in Adams County, the facility has listed Marc Feldman, Matthew Maurano, and Kevin Williams as its owners since Aug. 9, 2011.
The facility operates on a for-profit basis.
In that quarter, Transitions Healthcare Gettysburg held an overall CMS rating of 3, matching the Pennsylvania state nursing home average of 3.0. CMS assigns these ratings based on factors including health inspection reports, staffing metrics, and overall care quality provided to residents.
During the same period, Transitions Healthcare Gettysburg reported a daily average of 127.4 residents and had 135 available beds. The facility is not connected to a hospital.
For the first quarter of 2026, Transitions Healthcare Gettysburg incurred $16,334 in financial penalties after receiving two fines and facing two penalties in total.
There were three for-profit nursing homes located within Adams County, Pennsylvania.
Recent U.S. Census Bureau estimates indicate the population of older adults nationwide is growing as the number of younger individuals declines. Between 2020 and 2024, the group aged 65 and over was up by 13%, while residents under 18 decreased by 1.7%. In the past 100 years, the American older adult population has seen significant growth, increasing from 4.9 million in 1920 to over 61 million by 2024.
A study conducted in 2021 reported that nearly half, about 28 million people in this age group, could need long-term services and supports. The report further estimates that more than one third may eventually require nursing home care.
“Living a long life is something that many of us want and could get,” said Jesse Slome, executive director of the American Association for Long-Term Care Insurance, an industry education group. “But when we live a long life, the chances of us needing long-term care increase exponentially. But when you need that type of care, there are limited options.”
